items.title: 67395_Vic Dickenson oral history interview
items.q: Yes. We were pretty tight friends, you know.

ctx.x: Yeah, I used to listen to him ...(? )... There was another trumpet player back in those days, too -- Jabbo Smith. And there was one before Louis named Johnny Dunn, who I liked very much at the time. He used to the double-up time thing, you know, like the ...(? )... He'd do it with three majors and then double up the fourth one. [SINGS EXAMPLE] And it looked like every fourth chord he would just...he would double-time, you know. Playing notes that ...(? )... Solo.
Yeah, he did make a lot of records. He did things with the mutes, too.

items.title: 67395_Vic Dickenson oral history interview
items.q: We were pretty good tight friends, you know.

ctx.x: And as a composer he wrote songs. So -- what are you going to do?
You and Jabboe (PHONETIC) went together in the Claude Hopkins band.
Yeah. We were pretty good tight friends, you know. Yeah. Jabroe has written some several good numbers and no one has ever tried to do them. I did a couple of them.

He could play anything. I don't know why. This is several guys -- no one -- everyone seems to forget about. There's Rex Stewart. There's another guy was a genius on the trumpet. He really was. I mean I'm not taking anything away from anybody, but you know -- he was just a great guy.
Like Jethroe Smith (PHONETIC) was a great guy. Like Sidney Curtiss (PHONETIC) --
